func TestParseAllCheckpoints(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	tests := []struct {
		name    string
		message string
		want    []string
	}{
		{
			name:    "single checkpoint trailer",
			message: "Add feature\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: a1b2c3d4e5f6\n",
			want:    []string{"a1b2c3d4e5f6"},
		},
		{
			name:    "no trailer",
			message: "Simple commit message",
			want:    nil,
		},
		{
			name:    "checkpoint trailers outside final block are ignored",
			message: "Soph/test branch (#2)\n\n* random_letter script\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: 0aa0814d9839\n\n* random color\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: 33fb587b6fbb\n",
			want:    []string{"33fb587b6fbb"},
		},
		{
			name:    "duplicate checkpoint IDs are deduplicated",
			message: "Merge\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: a1b2c3d4e5f6\nEntire-Checkpoint: b2c3d4e5f6a1\nEntire-Checkpoint: a1b2c3d4e5f6\n",
			want:    []string{"a1b2c3d4e5f6", "b2c3d4e5f6a1"},
		},
		{
			name:    "invalid checkpoint IDs are skipped",
			message: "Merge\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: a1b2c3d4e5f6\nEntire-Checkpoint: tooshort\nEntire-Checkpoint: b2c3d4e5f6a1\n",
			want:    []string{"a1b2c3d4e5f6", "b2c3d4e5f6a1"},
		},
		{
			name:    "mixed with other trailers",
			message: "Merge\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: a1b2c3d4e5f6\nEntire-Session: session-1\nEntire-Checkpoint: b2c3d4e5f6a1\n",
			want:    []string{"a1b2c3d4e5f6", "b2c3d4e5f6a1"},
		},
		{
			name:    "mixed hex and ULID checkpoint trailers",
			message: "Squash (#3)\n\n* legacy\n\n* new\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: a1b2c3d4e5f6\nEntire-Checkpoint: 01KVBJCWYA4YW6J5M9GP655HZN\n",
			want:    []string{"a1b2c3d4e5f6", "01KVBJCWYA4YW6J5M9GP655HZN"},
		},
	}

	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Parallel()

			got := ParseAllCheckpoints(tt.message)
			if len(got) != len(tt.want) {
				t.Errorf("ParseAllCheckpoints() returned %d items, want %d", len(got), len(tt.want))
				t.Errorf("got: %v, want: %v", got, tt.want)
				return
			}
			for i, wantID := range tt.want {
				expectedID := checkpointID.MustCheckpointID(wantID)
				if got[i] != expectedID {
					t.Errorf("ParseAllCheckpoints()[%d] = %v, want %v", i, got[i], expectedID)
				}
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestPrepareCommitMsg_AmendPreservesExistingTrailer verifies that when amending
// a commit that already has an Entire-Checkpoint trailer, the trailer is preserved
// unchanged. source="commit" indicates an amend operation.
func TestPrepareCommitMsg_AmendPreservesExistingTrailer(t *testing.T) {
	dir := setupGitRepo(t)
	t.Chdir(dir)

	s := &ManualCommitStrategy{}

	sessionID := "test-session-amend-preserve"
	err := s.InitializeSession(context.Background(), sessionID, agent.AgentTypeClaudeCode, "", "", "")
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Write a commit message file that already has the trailer
	commitMsgFile := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "COMMIT_EDITMSG")
	existingMsg := "Original commit message\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: abc123def456\n"
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(commitMsgFile, []byte(existingMsg), 0o644))

	// Call PrepareCommitMsg with source="commit" (amend)
	err = s.PrepareCommitMsg(context.Background(), commitMsgFile, "commit")
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Read the file back and verify the trailer is still present
	content, err := os.ReadFile(commitMsgFile)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	cpID, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(string(content))
	assert.True(t, found, "trailer should still be present after amend")
	assert.Equal(t, "abc123def456", cpID.String(),
		"trailer should preserve the original checkpoint ID")
}

// TestPrepareCommitMsg_AmendRestoresTrailerFromLastCheckpointID verifies the amend
// bug fix: when a user does `git commit --amend -m "new message"`, the Entire-Checkpoint
// trailer is lost because the new message replaces the old one. PrepareCommitMsg restores
// the trailer from LastCheckpointID in session state.
func TestPrepareCommitMsg_AmendRestoresTrailerFromLastCheckpointID(t *testing.T) {
	dir := setupGitRepo(t)
	t.Chdir(dir)

	s := &ManualCommitStrategy{}

	sessionID := "test-session-amend-restore"
	err := s.InitializeSession(context.Background(), sessionID, agent.AgentTypeClaudeCode, "", "", "")
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Simulate state after condensation: LastCheckpointID is set
	state, err := s.loadSessionState(context.Background(), sessionID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NotNil(t, state)
	state.LastCheckpointID = id.CheckpointID("abc123def456")
	err = s.saveSessionState(context.Background(), state)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Write a commit message file with NO trailer (user did --amend -m "new message")
	commitMsgFile := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "COMMIT_EDITMSG")
	newMsg := "New amended message\n"
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(commitMsgFile, []byte(newMsg), 0o644))

	// Call PrepareCommitMsg with source="commit" (amend)
	err = s.PrepareCommitMsg(context.Background(), commitMsgFile, "commit")
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Read the file back - trailer should be restored from LastCheckpointID
	content, err := os.ReadFile(commitMsgFile)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	cpID, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(string(content))
	assert.True(t, found,
		"trailer should be restored from LastCheckpointID on amend")
	assert.Equal(t, "abc123def456", cpID.String(),
		"restored trailer should use LastCheckpointID value")
}

// TestPrepareCommitMsg_AmendNoTrailerNoLastCheckpointID verifies that when amending with
// no existing trailer and no LastCheckpointID in session state, no trailer is added.
// This is the case where the session has never been condensed yet.
func TestPrepareCommitMsg_AmendNoTrailerNoLastCheckpointID(t *testing.T) {
	dir := setupGitRepo(t)
	t.Chdir(dir)

	s := &ManualCommitStrategy{}

	sessionID := "test-session-amend-no-id"
	err := s.InitializeSession(context.Background(), sessionID, agent.AgentTypeClaudeCode, "", "", "")
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Verify LastCheckpointID is empty (default)
	state, err := s.loadSessionState(context.Background(), sessionID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NotNil(t, state)
	assert.Empty(t, state.LastCheckpointID, "LastCheckpointID should be empty by default")

	// Write a commit message file with NO trailer
	commitMsgFile := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "COMMIT_EDITMSG")
	newMsg := "Amended without any session context\n"
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(commitMsgFile, []byte(newMsg), 0o644))

	// Call PrepareCommitMsg with source="commit" (amend)
	err = s.PrepareCommitMsg(context.Background(), commitMsgFile, "commit")
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Read the file back - no trailer should be added
	content, err := os.ReadFile(commitMsgFile)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	_, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(string(content))
	assert.False(t, found,
		"no trailer should be added when LastCheckpointID is empty")

	// Message should be unchanged
	assert.Equal(t, newMsg, string(content),
		"commit message should be unchanged when no trailer to restore")
}

// TestPrepareCommitMsg_StaleTaskRecordOnly_NoTrailerButStillCondensable pins the
// split between "condensable" and "may claim a trailer". An IDLE session whose
// only content is a task record past idleWithTaskContent's 24h bound used to be
// stamped by the slow path (sessionHasNewContent says yes on HasTaskContent with
// no bound) and then refused by PostCommit's overlap check, leaving
// Entire-Checkpoint pointing at a checkpoint nothing ever wrote. The trailer is
// now bounded, but sessionHasNewContent deliberately is not: the record stays
// recognized content so the session's transcript-so-far still materializes at
// its eventual condensation rather than being stranded.
func TestPrepareCommitMsg_StaleTaskRecordOnly_NoTrailerButStillCondensable(t *testing.T) {
	dir := setupGitRepo(t)
	t.Chdir(dir)

	ctx := context.Background()
	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(dir)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	s := &ManualCommitStrategy{}
	worktreePath, err := paths.WorktreeRoot(ctx)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	worktreeID, err := paths.GetWorktreeID(worktreePath)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	head, err := repo.Head()
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Sole content: a record started 30h ago. No transcript, no files, no steps.
	state := &SessionState{
		SessionID:    "test-session-stale-record-only",
		BaseCommit:   head.Hash().String(),
		WorktreePath: worktreePath,
		WorktreeID:   worktreeID,
		StartedAt:    time.Now().Add(-30 * time.Hour),
		Phase:        session.PhaseIdle,
		AgentType:    agent.AgentTypeClaudeCode,
		TaskRecords: []session.TaskRecord{
			{ToolUseID: "toolu_stale1", AgentID: "agent-stale1", StartedAt: time.Now().Add(-30 * time.Hour)},
		},
	}
	require.NoError(t, s.saveSessionState(ctx, state))

	commitMsgFile := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "COMMIT_EDITMSG")
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(commitMsgFile, []byte("unrelated human commit\n"), 0o644))
	require.NoError(t, s.PrepareCommitMsg(ctx, commitMsgFile, ""))

	content, err := os.ReadFile(commitMsgFile)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	_, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(string(content))
	assert.False(t, found,
		"a session whose only content is a stale task record must not claim a trailer")

	hasNew, err := s.sessionHasNewContent(ctx, repo, state, contentCheckOpts{})
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.True(t, hasNew,
		"the stale record must remain condensable content so it is not stranded unmaterialized")
}

func TestParseAllCheckpoints(t *testing.T) {

	}{

			message: "Add feature\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: a1b2c3d4e5f6\n",
			want:    []string{"a1b2c3d4e5f6"},
		},
		{
			name:    "no trailer",
			message: "Simple commit message",
			want:    nil,
		},
		{
			name:    "checkpoint trailers outside final block are ignored",
			message: "Soph/test branch (#2)\n\n* random_letter script\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: 0aa0814d9839\n\n* random color\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: 33fb587b6fbb\n",
			want:    []string{"33fb587b6fbb"},

func TestParseCheckpoint(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	tests := []struct {
		name      string
		message   string
		wantID    string
		wantFound bool
	}{
		{
			name:      "valid checkpoint trailer",
			message:   "Add feature\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: a1b2c3d4e5f6\n",
			wantID:    "a1b2c3d4e5f6",
			wantFound: true,
		},
		{
			name:      "valid ULID checkpoint trailer",
			message:   "Add feature\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: 01KVBJCWYA4YW6J5M9GP655HZN\n",
			wantID:    "01KVBJCWYA4YW6J5M9GP655HZN",
			wantFound: true,
		},
		{
			name:      "no trailer",
			message:   "Simple commit message",
			wantID:    "",
			wantFound: false,
		},
		{
			name:      "trailer with extra spaces",
			message:   "Message\n\nEntire-Checkpoint:   a1b2c3d4e5f6   \n",
			wantID:    "a1b2c3d4e5f6",
			wantFound: true,
		},
		{
			name:      "too short checkpoint ID",
			message:   "Message\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: abc123\n",
			wantID:    "",
			wantFound: false,
		},
		{
			name:      "too long checkpoint ID",
			message:   "Message\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: a1b2c3d4e5f6789\n",
			wantID:    "",
			wantFound: false,
		},
		{
			name:      "invalid characters in checkpoint ID",
			message:   "Message\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: a1b2c3d4e5gg\n",
			wantID:    "",
			wantFound: false,
		},
		{
			name:      "uppercase hex rejected",
			message:   "Message\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: A1B2C3D4E5F6\n",
			wantID:    "",
			wantFound: false,
		},
		{
			name:      "checkpoint-like body line ignored",
			message:   "Message\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: a1b2c3d4e5f6\n\nSigned-off-by: Test User <test@example.com>\n",
			wantID:    "",
			wantFound: false,
		},
		{
			name:      "final trailer wins over checkpoint-like body line",
			message:   "Message\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: a1b2c3d4e5f6\n\nBody continues here.\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: b2c3d4e5f6a1\n",
			wantID:    "b2c3d4e5f6a1",
			wantFound: true,
		},
	}

	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Parallel()

			gotID, gotFound := ParseCheckpoint(tt.message)
			if gotFound != tt.wantFound {
				t.Errorf("ParseCheckpoint() found = %v, want %v", gotFound, tt.wantFound)
			}
			if gotID.String() != tt.wantID {
				t.Errorf("ParseCheckpoint() id = %v, want %v", gotID.String(), tt.wantID)
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestPrepareCommitMsg_AmendPreservesExistingTrailer verifies that when amending
// a commit that already has an Entire-Checkpoint trailer, the trailer is preserved
// unchanged. source="commit" indicates an amend operation.
func TestPrepareCommitMsg_AmendPreservesExistingTrailer(t *testing.T) {
	dir := setupGitRepo(t)
	t.Chdir(dir)

	s := &ManualCommitStrategy{}

	sessionID := "test-session-amend-preserve"
	err := s.InitializeSession(context.Background(), sessionID, agent.AgentTypeClaudeCode, "", "", "")
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Write a commit message file that already has the trailer
	commitMsgFile := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "COMMIT_EDITMSG")
	existingMsg := "Original commit message\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: abc123def456\n"
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(commitMsgFile, []byte(existingMsg), 0o644))

	// Call PrepareCommitMsg with source="commit" (amend)
	err = s.PrepareCommitMsg(context.Background(), commitMsgFile, "commit")
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Read the file back and verify the trailer is still present
	content, err := os.ReadFile(commitMsgFile)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	cpID, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(string(content))
	assert.True(t, found, "trailer should still be present after amend")
	assert.Equal(t, "abc123def456", cpID.String(),
		"trailer should preserve the original checkpoint ID")
}

// TestPrepareCommitMsg_AmendRestoresTrailerFromLastCheckpointID verifies the amend
// bug fix: when a user does `git commit --amend -m "new message"`, the Entire-Checkpoint
// trailer is lost because the new message replaces the old one. PrepareCommitMsg restores
// the trailer from LastCheckpointID in session state.
func TestPrepareCommitMsg_AmendRestoresTrailerFromLastCheckpointID(t *testing.T) {
	dir := setupGitRepo(t)
	t.Chdir(dir)

	s := &ManualCommitStrategy{}

	sessionID := "test-session-amend-restore"
	err := s.InitializeSession(context.Background(), sessionID, agent.AgentTypeClaudeCode, "", "", "")
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Simulate state after condensation: LastCheckpointID is set
	state, err := s.loadSessionState(context.Background(), sessionID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NotNil(t, state)
	state.LastCheckpointID = id.CheckpointID("abc123def456")
	err = s.saveSessionState(context.Background(), state)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Write a commit message file with NO trailer (user did --amend -m "new message")
	commitMsgFile := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "COMMIT_EDITMSG")
	newMsg := "New amended message\n"
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(commitMsgFile, []byte(newMsg), 0o644))

	// Call PrepareCommitMsg with source="commit" (amend)
	err = s.PrepareCommitMsg(context.Background(), commitMsgFile, "commit")
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Read the file back - trailer should be restored from LastCheckpointID
	content, err := os.ReadFile(commitMsgFile)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	cpID, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(string(content))
	assert.True(t, found,
		"trailer should be restored from LastCheckpointID on amend")
	assert.Equal(t, "abc123def456", cpID.String(),
		"restored trailer should use LastCheckpointID value")
}

// TestPrepareCommitMsg_AmendNoTrailerNoLastCheckpointID verifies that when amending with
// no existing trailer and no LastCheckpointID in session state, no trailer is added.
// This is the case where the session has never been condensed yet.
func TestPrepareCommitMsg_AmendNoTrailerNoLastCheckpointID(t *testing.T) {
	dir := setupGitRepo(t)
	t.Chdir(dir)

	s := &ManualCommitStrategy{}

	sessionID := "test-session-amend-no-id"
	err := s.InitializeSession(context.Background(), sessionID, agent.AgentTypeClaudeCode, "", "", "")
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Verify LastCheckpointID is empty (default)
	state, err := s.loadSessionState(context.Background(), sessionID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NotNil(t, state)
	assert.Empty(t, state.LastCheckpointID, "LastCheckpointID should be empty by default")

	// Write a commit message file with NO trailer
	commitMsgFile := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "COMMIT_EDITMSG")
	newMsg := "Amended without any session context\n"
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(commitMsgFile, []byte(newMsg), 0o644))

	// Call PrepareCommitMsg with source="commit" (amend)
	err = s.PrepareCommitMsg(context.Background(), commitMsgFile, "commit")
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Read the file back - no trailer should be added
	content, err := os.ReadFile(commitMsgFile)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	_, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(string(content))
	assert.False(t, found,
		"no trailer should be added when LastCheckpointID is empty")

	// Message should be unchanged
	assert.Equal(t, newMsg, string(content),
		"commit message should be unchanged when no trailer to restore")
}

// TestPrepareCommitMsg_StaleTaskRecordOnly_NoTrailerButStillCondensable pins the
// split between "condensable" and "may claim a trailer". An IDLE session whose
// only content is a task record past idleWithTaskContent's 24h bound used to be
// stamped by the slow path (sessionHasNewContent says yes on HasTaskContent with
// no bound) and then refused by PostCommit's overlap check, leaving
// Entire-Checkpoint pointing at a checkpoint nothing ever wrote. The trailer is
// now bounded, but sessionHasNewContent deliberately is not: the record stays
// recognized content so the session's transcript-so-far still materializes at
// its eventual condensation rather than being stranded.
func TestPrepareCommitMsg_StaleTaskRecordOnly_NoTrailerButStillCondensable(t *testing.T) {
	dir := setupGitRepo(t)
	t.Chdir(dir)

	ctx := context.Background()
	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(dir)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	s := &ManualCommitStrategy{}
	worktreePath, err := paths.WorktreeRoot(ctx)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	worktreeID, err := paths.GetWorktreeID(worktreePath)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	head, err := repo.Head()
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Sole content: a record started 30h ago. No transcript, no files, no steps.
	state := &SessionState{
		SessionID:    "test-session-stale-record-only",
		BaseCommit:   head.Hash().String(),
		WorktreePath: worktreePath,
		WorktreeID:   worktreeID,
		StartedAt:    time.Now().Add(-30 * time.Hour),
		Phase:        session.PhaseIdle,
		AgentType:    agent.AgentTypeClaudeCode,
		TaskRecords: []session.TaskRecord{
			{ToolUseID: "toolu_stale1", AgentID: "agent-stale1", StartedAt: time.Now().Add(-30 * time.Hour)},
		},
	}
	require.NoError(t, s.saveSessionState(ctx, state))

	commitMsgFile := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "COMMIT_EDITMSG")
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(commitMsgFile, []byte("unrelated human commit\n"), 0o644))
	require.NoError(t, s.PrepareCommitMsg(ctx, commitMsgFile, ""))

	content, err := os.ReadFile(commitMsgFile)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	_, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(string(content))
	assert.False(t, found,
		"a session whose only content is a stale task record must not claim a trailer")

	hasNew, err := s.sessionHasNewContent(ctx, repo, state, contentCheckOpts{})
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.True(t, hasNew,
		"the stale record must remain condensable content so it is not stranded unmaterialized")
}

func TestParseAllCheckpoints(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	tests := []struct {
		name    string
		message string
		want    []string
	}{
		{
			name:    "single checkpoint trailer",
			message: "Add feature\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: a1b2c3d4e5f6\n",
			want:    []string{"a1b2c3d4e5f6"},
		},
		{
			name:    "no trailer",
			message: "Simple commit message",
			want:    nil,
		},
		{
			name:    "checkpoint trailers outside final block are ignored",
			message: "Soph/test branch (#2)\n\n* random_letter script\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: 0aa0814d9839\n\n* random color\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: 33fb587b6fbb\n",
			want:    []string{"33fb587b6fbb"},
		},
		{
			name:    "duplicate checkpoint IDs are deduplicated",
			message: "Merge\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: a1b2c3d4e5f6\nEntire-Checkpoint: b2c3d4e5f6a1\nEntire-Checkpoint: a1b2c3d4e5f6\n",
			want:    []string{"a1b2c3d4e5f6", "b2c3d4e5f6a1"},
		},
		{
			name:    "invalid checkpoint IDs are skipped",
			message: "Merge\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: a1b2c3d4e5f6\nEntire-Checkpoint: tooshort\nEntire-Checkpoint: b2c3d4e5f6a1\n",
			want:    []string{"a1b2c3d4e5f6", "b2c3d4e5f6a1"},
		},
		{
			name:    "mixed with other trailers",
			message: "Merge\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: a1b2c3d4e5f6\nEntire-Session: session-1\nEntire-Checkpoint: b2c3d4e5f6a1\n",
			want:    []string{"a1b2c3d4e5f6", "b2c3d4e5f6a1"},
		},
		{
			name:    "mixed hex and ULID checkpoint trailers",
			message: "Squash (#3)\n\n* legacy\n\n* new\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: a1b2c3d4e5f6\nEntire-Checkpoint: 01KVBJCWYA4YW6J5M9GP655HZN\n",
			want:    []string{"a1b2c3d4e5f6", "01KVBJCWYA4YW6J5M9GP655HZN"},
		},
	}

	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Parallel()

			got := ParseAllCheckpoints(tt.message)
			if len(got) != len(tt.want) {
				t.Errorf("ParseAllCheckpoints() returned %d items, want %d", len(got), len(tt.want))
				t.Errorf("got: %v, want: %v", got, tt.want)
				return
			}
			for i, wantID := range tt.want {
				expectedID := checkpointID.MustCheckpointID(wantID)
				if got[i] != expectedID {
					t.Errorf("ParseAllCheckpoints()[%d] = %v, want %v", i, got[i], expectedID)
				}
			}
		})
	}
}

			wantFound: true,

			name:      "no trailer",
			message:   "Simple commit message",
			wantID:    "",
			wantFound: false,
		},
		{
			name:      "trailer with extra spaces",
			message:   "Message\n\nEntire-Checkpoint:   a1b2c3d4e5f6   \n",
			wantID:    "a1b2c3d4e5f6",
			wantFound: true,
		},
		{
			name:      "too short checkpoint ID",
			message:   "Message\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: abc123\n",
			wantID:    "",
			wantFound: false,
		},

			name:      "too long checkpoint ID",
			message:   "Message\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: a1b2c3d4e5f6789\n",
			wantID:    "",
			wantFound: false,
		},
		{
			name:      "invalid characters in checkpoint ID",
			message:   "Message\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: a1b2c3d4e5gg\n",
			wantID:    "",
			wantFound: false,
		},
		{
			name:      "uppercase hex rejected",
			message:   "Message\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: A1B2C3D4E5F6\n",
			wantID:    "",
			wantFound: false,

		{
			name:      "checkpoint-like body line ignored",

			wantID:    "",

		},
		{
			name:      "final trailer wins over checkpoint-like body line",
			message:   "Message\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: a1b2c3d4e5f6\n\nBody continues here.\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: b2c3d4e5f6a1\n",
			wantID:    "b2c3d4e5f6a1",
			wantFound: true,
		},
	}

	for _, tt := range tests {

			t.Parallel()

			if gotFound != tt.wantFound {

				t.Errorf("ParseCheckpoint() id = %v, want %v", gotID.String(), tt.wantID)
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestPrepareCommitMsg_StaleTaskRecordOnly_NoTrailerButStillCondensable pins the
// split between "condensable" and "may claim a trailer". An IDLE session whose
// only content is a task record past idleWithTaskContent's 24h bound used to be
// stamped by the slow path (sessionHasNewContent says yes on HasTaskContent with
// no bound) and then refused by PostCommit's overlap check, leaving
// Entire-Checkpoint pointing at a checkpoint nothing ever wrote. The trailer is
// now bounded, but sessionHasNewContent deliberately is not: the record stays
// recognized content so the session's transcript-so-far still materializes at
// its eventual condensation rather than being stranded.
func TestPrepareCommitMsg_StaleTaskRecordOnly_NoTrailerButStillCondensable(t *testing.T) {
	dir := setupGitRepo(t)
	t.Chdir(dir)

	ctx := context.Background()
	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(dir)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	s := &ManualCommitStrategy{}
	worktreePath, err := paths.WorktreeRoot(ctx)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	worktreeID, err := paths.GetWorktreeID(worktreePath)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	head, err := repo.Head()
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Sole content: a record started 30h ago. No transcript, no files, no steps.
	state := &SessionState{
		SessionID:    "test-session-stale-record-only",
		BaseCommit:   head.Hash().String(),
		WorktreePath: worktreePath,
		WorktreeID:   worktreeID,
		StartedAt:    time.Now().Add(-30 * time.Hour),
		Phase:        session.PhaseIdle,
		AgentType:    agent.AgentTypeClaudeCode,
		TaskRecords: []session.TaskRecord{
			{ToolUseID: "toolu_stale1", AgentID: "agent-stale1", StartedAt: time.Now().Add(-30 * time.Hour)},
		},
	}
	require.NoError(t, s.saveSessionState(ctx, state))

	commitMsgFile := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "COMMIT_EDITMSG")
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(commitMsgFile, []byte("unrelated human commit\n"), 0o644))
	require.NoError(t, s.PrepareCommitMsg(ctx, commitMsgFile, ""))

	content, err := os.ReadFile(commitMsgFile)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	_, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(string(content))
	assert.False(t, found,
		"a session whose only content is a stale task record must not claim a trailer")

	hasNew, err := s.sessionHasNewContent(ctx, repo, state, contentCheckOpts{})
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.True(t, hasNew,
		"the stale record must remain condensable content so it is not stranded unmaterialized")
}

func TestParseAllCheckpoints(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()

	tests := []struct {
		name    string
		message string
		want    []string
	}{
		{
			name:    "single checkpoint trailer",
			message: "Add feature\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: a1b2c3d4e5f6\n",
			want:    []string{"a1b2c3d4e5f6"},
		},
		{
			name:    "no trailer",
			message: "Simple commit message",
			want:    nil,
		},
		{
			name:    "checkpoint trailers outside final block are ignored",
			message: "Soph/test branch (#2)\n\n* random_letter script\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: 0aa0814d9839\n\n* random color\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: 33fb587b6fbb\n",
			want:    []string{"33fb587b6fbb"},
		},
		{
			name:    "duplicate checkpoint IDs are deduplicated",
			message: "Merge\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: a1b2c3d4e5f6\nEntire-Checkpoint: b2c3d4e5f6a1\nEntire-Checkpoint: a1b2c3d4e5f6\n",
			want:    []string{"a1b2c3d4e5f6", "b2c3d4e5f6a1"},
		},
		{
			name:    "invalid checkpoint IDs are skipped",
			message: "Merge\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: a1b2c3d4e5f6\nEntire-Checkpoint: tooshort\nEntire-Checkpoint: b2c3d4e5f6a1\n",
			want:    []string{"a1b2c3d4e5f6", "b2c3d4e5f6a1"},
		},
		{
			name:    "mixed with other trailers",
			message: "Merge\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: a1b2c3d4e5f6\nEntire-Session: session-1\nEntire-Checkpoint: b2c3d4e5f6a1\n",
			want:    []string{"a1b2c3d4e5f6", "b2c3d4e5f6a1"},
		},
		{
			name:    "mixed hex and ULID checkpoint trailers",
			message: "Squash (#3)\n\n* legacy\n\n* new\n\nEntire-Checkpoint: a1b2c3d4e5f6\nEntire-Checkpoint: 01KVBJCWYA4YW6J5M9GP655HZN\n",
			want:    []string{"a1b2c3d4e5f6", "01KVBJCWYA4YW6J5M9GP655HZN"},
		},
	}

	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			t.Parallel()

			got := ParseAllCheckpoints(tt.message)
			if len(got) != len(tt.want) {
				t.Errorf("ParseAllCheckpoints() returned %d items, want %d", len(got), len(tt.want))
				t.Errorf("got: %v, want: %v", got, tt.want)
				return
			}
			for i, wantID := range tt.want {
				expectedID := checkpointID.MustCheckpointID(wantID)
				if got[i] != expectedID {
					t.Errorf("ParseAllCheckpoints()[%d] = %v, want %v", i, got[i], expectedID)
				}
			}
		})
	}
}

# Verify Tests

After writing tests, verify they are genuine — testing real code paths with real inputs and outputs, not mocked-out logic that trivially passes. Guards against the failure mode where tests appear to pass but test nothing meaningful.

## When to Use

- **Invoke** (`/verify-tests`) after writing new tests in a session
- **AI should suggest** when: tests are written, user says "verify tests", "check tests pass", "make sure tests work", or after completing a `/prd` task that included test writing

## Process

### Step 1: Run the Tests — Always With Output Visible

**Always use output flags. No exceptions.**

```bash
cargo test <module> -- --nocapture      # Rust — shows println! and test output
pytest <test_file> -v -s               # Python — shows print() statements
npm test -- --verbose                  # JavaScript — shows console.log
vitest run --reporter=verbose          # Vitest
```

Do not proceed if any tests fail — fix them first.

### Step 2: Show Inputs and Outputs for Every Test

For each test, explicitly show:

- **Test name**
- **What is actually being called** (the real function — not a mock or reimplemented version)
- **Input**: exact values passed in
- **Expected output**: what the test asserts
- **Actual output**: what was actually returned (from `--nocapture` / `-s`)

Example format:

```
Test: test_empty_input_returns_empty
Function: <RealModule>::<real_method> (not mocked)
Input: empty list []
Expected: []
Actual: [] ✓
```

### Step 3: Check for Anti-Patterns

Flag any of these:

- [ ] **Recreated logic in tests** — the test imports and calls the real function, not a reimplemented version of it
- [ ] **Over-mocking** — only external service boundaries should be mocked (network, cloud API, file I/O); core logic should be real
- [ ] **Trivial assertions** — `assert result is not None` tells you nothing; assert the actual value
- [ ] **Hallucinated passing** — test passes because of a loose assertion, not because the code is correct
- [ ] **Happy path only** — edge cases (empty input, boundaries, errors) must also be covered

### Step 4: Report

```markdown
## Test Verification Report

### Tests Run: <N>
### All Passing: ✓ / ✗

| Test | Real Function Called | Input | Expected | Actual | Pass |
|------|---------------------|-------|----------|--------|------|
| test_name | Module::method | <input> | <expected> | <actual> | ✓ |

### Anti-Patterns Found
- None ✓  (or list findings)

### Verdict
Tests are genuine and meaningful. / Issues found — see above.
```

## Rules

- **Always run tests before verifying** — never review test code without running it
- **Show actual output** — use `--nocapture` / `-s` so you can see what the code actually returns
- **Import real modules** — if a test reimplements logic to test it, it tests nothing
- **Mock only at boundaries** — network, cloud APIs, file I/O. Never mock core domain logic.
- **"Tests pass" is not enough** — show which tests, with what inputs, producing what outputs

---
name: commit
description: Stage changes and commit with a properly formatted conventional commit message. Optionally push. Use when the user says commit / checkpoint this, when completing a task, or after any substantial change. Always use this skill to commit — never run git commit directly.
user-invocable: true
disable-model-invocation: false
---

# Commit

Stage relevant changes and create a commit using the conventional commits format.
Always use this skill instead of running `git commit` directly — this ensures
the message format is consistent across every tool (OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex).

## When to Use

- **Invoke** (`/commit`) after completing every task — this is the final step of every task
- **Invoke** (`/commit --push`) to commit and push in one step
- **AI must use this skill** whenever a commit is needed — never run `git commit -m` directly
- **AI should suggest** when: user says "commit", "save my changes", "checkpoint",
  "commit this", "commit and push", "push my changes", or a task's acceptance criteria say "committed using /commit skill"

## Commit Message Format

```
<type>(<scope>): <description>
```

**Types:**
- `feat` — new feature or capability
- `fix` — bug fix
- `chore` — build, config, dependency, tooling change (no production code change)
- `docs` — documentation only
- `test` — adding or updating tests
- `refactor` — code restructuring with no behaviour change
- `perf` — performance improvement

**Scope** is derived from the project structure. Use the most descriptive scope for the files changed. Scope is optional for small repos or when the change spans the whole repo.

**Examples:**
```
feat(api): add pagination to list endpoint
fix(auth): handle expired refresh tokens
test(search): add round-trip tests for index serialization
chore(ci): update release workflow
refactor(core): extract filter logic into separate function
docs: update CHANGELOG for new feature
```

## Steps

1. Run `git status` to see all changed/untracked files
2. Run `git diff --staged` (or `git diff` if nothing staged) to understand exactly what changed
3. Group related files — do not commit unrelated changes in one commit
4. Stage the relevant files: `git add <specific files>`
5. Draft a commit message following the format above
6. Show the message to the user and confirm before committing
7. Run `git commit -m "<message>"`

### Optional: Push (when `--push` is passed or user asks to push)

---
name: progress-update
description: Update local-only task/progress files after a completed task so the next agent session can resume instantly without treating shared files as coordination locks.
user-invocable: true
disable-model-invocation: false
---

# Progress Update

Append one entry to the progress file documenting this session's work — concrete enough that a
fresh agent reading it cold knows exactly where to pick up. The file is append-only; entries grow
downward and are numbered sequentially.

Use when: after every completed task (per-task loop: verify → commit → progress). Run it automatically after `/commit` on a completed task — don't wait to be asked.

Output file: the progress file in the current task worktree, usually `progress.md`. In parallel mode, never write to another task worktree's progress file and never treat edits to shared `tasks.md` as an atomic lock.

## Do

1. **Verify commits exist first.** `git log --oneline -10`; every completed task must have a
   commit. If one is done but uncommitted, tell the user to run `/commit` first and stop.
2. **Gather** (from the session or by asking): tasks completed, decisions + *why*, files touched,
   tests added/run and results, the next task.
3. **Append the entry** at the bottom, incrementing the session number. Decisions must explain the
   why, not just the what. Always include a concrete test count. Next steps are explicit (task ID
   + title + priority) so the next agent starts immediately.
4. **Update only local coordination state.** If this worktree has `task.md`, mark it done. If it has a local copy of `tasks.md`, you may mark the assigned task done there for readability, but this is not authoritative across parallel agents.
5. **Keep coordination files local.** Never stage, commit, or push `task.md`, `problems.md`, `tasks.md`, `progress.md`, or any `progress-*.md` file unless the user explicitly says these files are meant to be versioned.
6. **Leave central status to the integrator.** After a task branch is merged back into the base feature branch, the coordinator/integrator updates the base `tasks.md` in dependency order.

## Output

```markdown
### Session <N> - <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM TZ>

Completed Tasks:
- PREFIX-001: <title>
  <what was built — 1-3 specific sentences; explain any decision inline>

Tech Notes:
- <decision + rationale; gotchas or deviations from plan>

Tests: <N> tests passing. <test command>

Next Steps:
- PREFIX-003: <title> (P1)
- PREFIX-004: <title> (P1) — blocked until PREFIX-003

---
```

Stop after updating the local coordination files. Never edit existing progress entries — only append.

## Review findings and recommendation

The issue is real, but final-block-only parsing everywhere is incompatible with supported squash-resume behavior. Legitimate GitHub and native Git squash messages place original checkpoint trailers in body paragraphs.

Recommendation: narrow and evolve the experiment.

- Whole-message parsing remains for historical discovery and squash resume.
- New final-trailer-block APIs guard checkpoint creation, mutation, and reuse.
- Commit hooks and attach now ignore checkpoint-shaped body text.
- Storage existence validates discovered resume candidates, but cannot authenticate them. Fully eliminating that ambiguity would require a new authenticated checkpoint-to-commit association or removing squash-body discovery.

PR [#2168](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2168) remains open, so its broader line-anchoring work was not assumed or duplicated.

## Patch summary

- Added strict final-block parsers in [trailers.go](/Users/muskanpaliwal/Work/open-source/entire/cli/fix-checkpoint-trailer-block/cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go:150).
- Applied them to commit hooks, including Git comment-block handling, in [manual_commit_hooks.go](/Users/muskanpaliwal/Work/open-source/entire/cli/fix-checkpoint-trailer-block/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go:290).
- Prevented attach from reusing checkpoint-shaped body text in [attach.go](/Users/muskanpaliwal/Work/open-source/entire/cli/fix-checkpoint-trailer-block/cmd/entire/cli/attach.go:651).
- Added production-boundary regressions in [manual_commit_worktree_session_test.go](/Users/muskanpaliwal/Work/open-source/entire/cli/fix-checkpoint-trailer-block/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_worktree_session_test.go:54) and [attach_test.go](/Users/muskanpaliwal/Work/open-source/entire/cli/fix-checkpoint-trailer-block/cmd/entire/cli/attach_test.go:2021).
- Preserved the original real squash fixtures and historical parsing behavior.

## Validation

- Focused parser, hook, attach, and all three named squash-resume unit tests passed.
- `TestResumeSquashMergeMultipleCheckpoints` passed for Vogon and roger-roger.
- First `mise run check` encountered the unrelated mirror timeout flake; isolated reproduction passed 10/10.
- Subsequent full `mise run check` runs passed completely, including 56 Vogon and 4 roger-roger canaries.
- No paid real-agent E2E tests were run.

- Seven scoped files are staged; nothing was pushed or posted publicly.
